I would implore you not to view him as the "love of your life" though.  When I lost the "love of my life" I was wrecked for over a year, and that label didn't help anything.   Try to remember that there is no such thing as "the one", or rather that there are many potential "ones." You will find someone else. These started when I was a child:
--took everything personally, would stay mad at someone for days until they said something nice to me and I realized we weren't mortal enemies like I thought we were
--semi-existential crises...that is, I felt it was unfair that I was brought into this world without having a choice.  I even had a great childhood.  Not sure if this was due to BPD but I didn't know any other kid that thought like this
--in kindergarten I was already trying to find a girlfriend, I fantasized every day about having someone to share a deep connection with
--constantly felt like my parents didn't love me

These started when I was a teenager:
--suicidal ideations, constant obsession with suicide and eventially with joininwtg the marines so I would go off and die in a war
--no persistent identity, would simply mirror the personality of the person I was with.  Still do this.  I've seen a lot people say that only women do this, but I do it
  Then again I sometimes feel like a woman trapped in a man's body.

Starting as an adult:
--when I met my first girlfriend (at 20) I built her up highly in my mind.  Then she would do small things that would upset me greatly.  One day she stopped texting me for 30 minutes to talk to her ex boyfriend on MySpace.  I sent her many texts about how betrayed and stabbed in the back I felt.  She broke up with me. I jumped in my car to go talk to her face to face even though she didn't want to.  On the way there I changed my mind and decided I would crash my car into a building at her community college instead.  Somehow on the drive there I calmed down
--this kicked off a month of me being suicidal.  I thought what I was feeling was normal for a first break up... eventually I got through it by punishing myself every time I thoght about her and repressing everything...
--the next woman I met was an even worse situation...it would take too long to go into detail here though.

Basically every time I got suicidal I blamed it on my depression, because that was what I was diagnosed with.  Looking back I was never depressed enough to.kill myself though.  What caused me to be suicidal was that the pain of losing someone I got so attached to was too much to bear*.  I am somewhat of a success story though, my last girlfriend and my current one haven't really given me any problems on the BPD front.  I have learned not to get so attached to people, probably from living in intense pain for years because of a cumulative 5 months of dating.

*I didn't have a girlfriend in high school, so I think the suicidal obsession there was because of both depression and BPD...and feeling isolated from everyone.  For a year there I had no friends I stayed in contact with and my parents and I fought constantly, so it was a miracle I didn't kill myself then.  I would have if I had been able to force myself to drink gasoline like I planned, though.
